title: Post-Promotional Interest Charges on Home Comfort Financing Accounts
content:
On a Home Comfort Financing promotional plan whose promotion has ended, the balance left accrues post-promotional interest, posted once for each statement period as an interest charge on the first day after that period's statement closes.

This applies to the 12-Month Same-As-Cash Deferred Interest Plan and the 18-Month and 36-Month 0% APR Equal Payment Plans once the promotional end date has passed. Each statement period after the promotion carries one post-promotional interest charge, and the charge appears on that month's statement as an interest line.

## The fee position the charge is measured on

The post-promotional interest charge for a statement period is worked out only after the account carries the late fee owed for that same period whenever its installment stayed unpaid past its grace period, so that the interest base is measured on the period's closed fee position.

Read against the account's records: for a statement period whose installment stayed unpaid past its grace period, the period's post-promotional interest charge waits until that period's late fee is on the account; for a period whose installment did not stay unpaid past its grace period, the charge has no such wait.

## Posting the charge: `post_post_promo_interest_b0f5a17d`

**Capability.** `post_post_promo_interest_b0f5a17d` posts the post-promotional interest charge on a Home Comfort Financing account whose promotional period has ended, for one closed statement month. The charge is added to the amount the borrower owes, appears on that month's statement as an interest line dated today, and the account balance rises by the same amount. It books the amount it is given.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `post_post_promo_interest_b0f5a17d` and then calls it.

**Parameters.**

- `finance_account_id` — reference number of the financing account the interest is charged to, as shown by the financing account lookup for the verified borrower.
- `statement_period` — the closed statement month the interest charge belongs to, written YYYY-MM (four-digit year, hyphen, two-digit month, e.g. 2026-04), in Eastern time.
- `amount` — the interest charge to post, in USD, 2 decimal places, always positive, already rounded to the cent.

**Return.** The receipt carries `finance_txn_id` (reference number of the new interest line), `line_type` (always "interest"), `statement_period` (YYYY-MM month the charge was posted to), `amount` (USD, 2 decimal places), `posted_date` (YYYY-MM-DD posting date), `account_balance` (USD, 2 decimal places, the balance owed after the charge) and `status`, which reads "posted" when the charge is on the account.

## Q&A

**Does a fixed-rate account take this charge?** No. This charge belongs to promotional plans whose promotion has ended; fixed-rate plans have no promotional period.

**How often does it post?** Once for each statement period, on the first day after that period's statement closes — the first day of the following month, since statements close on the last day of the calendar month.
